abstract:
Abstract
                  As domestic robots move into the privacy-sensitive spaces of the home, pinpointing the design cues that shape acceptance becomes critical. Our $3\times 3\times 3$ mixed factorial experiment ($N=60$) shows that robot autonomy alone does not undermine privacy: contrary to expectations, autonomous housekeepers were perceived as safer and generated lower privacy concern than passive, command-only robots ($p&lt;.001$). Communication style mattered more than autonomy: shifting from direct to highly obscure communication about privacy-relevant actions consistently improved perceived safety and reduced privacy concern across all robot roles and scenarios (all $p&lt;.001$), with the largest gains found for autonomous robots operating in monitoring/surveillance contexts (three-way interaction, $p=.007$), while age, gender, and technology background further moderated these effects. Together, the findings suggest that privacy-conscious domestic robot design should focus less on constraining robot autonomy and more on how robots communicate about privacy-sensitive actions, particularly in monitoring contexts.

ur.ai_reason: 机器人角色与沟通方式影响隐私感知和接纳
ur.tldr: 家庭服务机器人实验显示，自主性并非隐私顾虑主因；相较仅接受指令的机器人，自主管家反而被感知为更安全。采用高度隐晦的隐私相关沟通可提升安全感知并降低担忧，效果在监控情境中最明显，且受年龄、性别和技术背景调节。

title: Navigating privacy in smart homes: how robot roles, communication styles, and contextual scenarios shape user perceptions of domestic service robots
title_zh: 智能家居中的隐私：机器人角色、沟通与情境如何影响用户对家用服务机器人的感知
